title: Nucleophilic Addition Reactions: One Carbonyl, Five Pathways
subject: Chemistry
objective: Every nucleophilic addition reaction of aldehydes and ketones in one place: HCN, NaHSO₃, Grignard reagents, alcohols, and the addition–elimination of ammonia derivatives, with the product each one gives.

fill.q: With HCN, the species that actually attacks the carbonyl carbon is ____.
An aldehyde with NaHSO₃ gives a crystalline ____ addition compound.
A ketone with a Grignard reagent, then H₃O⁺, gives a ____ alcohol.
One molecule of alcohol adds to an aldehyde to give a ____.
NH₂OH converts an aldehyde or ketone into an ____.

tf.q: Pure HCN adds to carbonyl compounds very slowly; a base speeds it up.
tf.explain: The base makes CN⁻, the stronger nucleophile.

tf.q: In the bisulphite adduct, the HSO₃⁻ ion bonds to carbon through its oxygen.
Formaldehyde with CH₃MgBr, then H₃O⁺, gives a primary alcohol.
The reaction of carbonyl compounds with H₂N–Z is a simple addition.
tf.explain: It is addition followed by loss of water: addition–elimination.

ar.a: Ketones give the bisulphite addition compound less readily than aldehydes.
ar.r: The two alkyl groups crowd the carbonyl carbon.

ar.a: 2,4-DNP gives a coloured precipitate with aldehydes and ketones.
ar.r: The C=O group becomes C=N–NHC₆H₃(NO₂)₂ with loss of water.

mcq.explain: CN and OH on the same carbon: a cyanohydrin.

mcq.q: Which gives a 2° alcohol with CH₃MgBr, then H₃O⁺?
An acetal has on one carbon:
mcq.explain: Hemiacetal: OH + OR; acetal: OR + OR.

num.q: How many carbon groups are on the OH-bearing carbon of the alcohol from acetone + CH₃MgBr?
How many molecules of CH₃OH are used to turn one CH₃CHO into its acetal?
steps: One gives the hemiacetal, the second the acetal

short.q: Write the products of CH₃CHO with (i) HCN (ii) NH₂OH (iii) 2 CH₃OH in dry HCl, and name each.
short.solution: (i) CH₃CH(OH)CN, a cyanohydrin (ii) CH₃CH=NOH, an oxime (iii) CH₃CH(OCH₃)₂, an acetal
